subject: rain falling
title: What If You Drank Rainwater?

scenes.text: What if you drank rain straight from the sky? Even the cleanest rain on Earth fails one test.
On the way down, rain washes dust, smoke and pollution out of the air.
Collect it off a roof, and it can pick up bird droppings, germs and metals like lead from the gutters.
In 2022, scientists reviewed rain measurements from around the world for PFAS, the so-called forever chemicals.
Even on the remote Tibetan Plateau, rain held about fourteen times the US safety advisory for one of them, set that year.
Their conclusion: under that advisory, rain everywhere on Earth would count as unsafe to drink. And these chemicals take decades to centuries to wash away.

description:
What if you drank rainwater? Rain picks up dust and pollution as it falls, and roofs and gutters can add bird droppings, germs and metals such as lead, which is why the CDC advises against drinking untreated collected rain.
A 2022 Stockholm University review (Environmental Science & Technology) found PFOA in rain even on the remote Tibetan Plateau at about 14 times the US EPA's 2022 lifetime health advisory, concluding rainwater everywhere would be judged unsafe under it. (In 2024 the EPA replaced that advisory with an enforceable limit of 4 parts per trillion.)
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Even Antarctic rain carries these chemicals. Have you ever drunk rainwater? What should we run through next?
